headline: Universal Quantum, a University of Sussex spinout, has raised $100 million in a round it calls the largest of its kind for a UK quantum firm.
score_reason: A large funding round for a quantum firm, reported with the company's own record-size claim.
importance_line: What changed: a UK quantum start-up has raised $100 million from investors including DCVC and Firgun Ventures to expand in the US, Japan and Germany, but the 'largest' claim and the technical promises come from the company and no outside check is reported.
summary: Tech.eu reports that Universal Quantum, founded in 2018 as a University of Sussex spinout, has raised $100 million in a Series A round (an early-stage funding round), which the company says is the largest of its kind for a UK-headquartered quantum firm. The round was co-led by the Silicon Valley venture firm DCVC and the quantum-focused investor Firgun Ventures, and the money will fund expansion in the US, Japan and Germany and the commercialisation of its quantum computing technology.
notes: Full text read on Tech.eu. Company statements kept hedged. Pool score 6 kept (funding round for a quantum firm).
